name: Redken

lead:
Redken is a professional hair care brand founded in 1960 that sells shampoo, conditioner, treatments, hair colour and styling products. It is distributed through salons and is owned by L'Oreal. People use it to improve the look of damaged, coloured or fine hair: smoother, shinier and more manageable strands.
The brand grew from a protein-and-acidic-pH approach to hair care, and later lines include bond-repair concentrates and blonde-toning products. Published research on specific Redken products is lacking, so claims come from the company and stylists.

paras: Users apply shampoo and conditioner in their usual routine and use treatments or styling products as directed on labels. Colour lines are applied by stylists. Products are sold through salons and retailers.
Like other hair products, ingredients can cause scalp or skin irritation or allergic reactions in some people; bleach and colour products need patch testing per manufacturer labels.

lead: Redken is an American professional hair care brand that makes shampoos, conditioners, styling products and colour treatments, sold mainly through salons.[1][2] It is used by people who want healthier-looking, shinier, more manageable or colour-treated hair.

The brand was founded in 1960 by actress Paula Kent and hairdresser Jheri Redding, with its name drawn from their surnames, and promoted a "Scientific Approach to Beauty" built around protein reconditioning and acid-balanced formulas.[1][2] In 1993, with sales of about $160 million, it was sold to Cosmair, the US licensee of L'Oreal, which L'Oreal fully acquired in 1994.[1][2]

Marketing has used public faces, including Lea T in 2014, Suki Waterhouse in 2015 and Sabrina Carpenter, named first global ambassador in 2024.[1] Its Blondage line targets colour-correcting hair to blonde.[1]
infobox: Blondage, Acidic Bonding Concentrate, All Soft

paras: Kent, who had fine hair and sensitive skin, worked with Redding to develop gentler hair products; the first lines included Amino Pon and the Protein Protein Treatment, according to the brand history.[2] Kent bought out Redding in 1965 and the company went public in 1971.[2]
Lines include Acidic Bonding Concentrate for bond repair and All Soft for hydration, plus vegan colour formulas.[2]
